messages:
sara: Follow-up from today's RFC sync: proposing a lightweight Precision Declaration layer that lives above legacy quant profiles. Purpose: make runtime decision simple and let policy live in a versioned object store.

jia: Quick Q: how is this different from the "intent" idea we saw? Need to clarify naming and surface area.

sara: Difference: "declaration" is intended as authoritative policy per-route/tenant. It declares acceptable precisions + constraints. Runtime only performs a fast match and emits a result. Intent was more client-driven; declaration is server-side policy-first.

mike: From infra POV we like server-side policies. Less per-request metadata to parse. But we still need a cheap negotiation header so legacy clients can opt-in.

alan: Concrete schema sketch (text):
{
  "api": "precision-decl.v1",
  "id": "fast-path-lowlatency",
  "allowed": ["fp8","int8","4bit"],
  "min_quality_score": "0.98",    // fraction vs gold baseline
  "stability": "soft|hard",      // soft allows runtime fallback, hard forbids
  "hw_profiles": {"a100": "perf_range:1.6-1.9","p4d": "perf_range:1.7-2.0"},
  "override_policy": "customer_readonly|allow_with_approval"
}

lucy: please avoid nested objects in the public API, but internal storage can be structured. Also call out per-tenant overrides for enterprise.

mike: Perf numbers we've measured (short seqs):
- fp8 ~ 1.7x tokens/sec vs int8 on p4d
- 4bit ~ 2.7x but 4bit shows up to 8% variance in tail latency
We should include a perf bucket per hw class in the declaration for SLO calc.

jia: Observability plan: emit these fields in telemetry: declaration_id, chosen_precision, baseline_score, observed_score, quality_delta, latency_p50/p95, hw_class. That will let Optimize compute per-declaration economics.

alan: Compatibility/migration plan:
- translate existing quant profiles to best-effort declarations in a migration job
- runtime will accept both old profile header and declaration id; precedence: declaration id > header > default profile
- canary flow: route 2% traffic with declaration enforcement and shadow baseline on 100% traffic for 72h
- rollback: declarations flagged with quick_disable true can be toggled via rwctl

sara: Example runtime header handshake we prefer:
// client -> runtime
X-Declaration-Id: fast-path-lowlatency

// runtime -> client (quick headers)
X-Chosen-Precision: fp8
X-Precision-Reason: matches_decl + capacity_ok

mike: runtime should also include a short code for reason (e.g., 0=match,1=fallback_capacity,2=fallback_quality). That keeps tracing parsable.

lucy: On admin side, we need an approval workflow for enterprise overrides. Suggest adding an approvals field: approvers: [email list], expiry.

jia: Test plan: small eval corpus per-customer to compute baseline_score. Add unit tests to fail if quality_delta > (1 - min_quality_score). Also add an end-to-end shadow harness that runs selected precision against baseline in background and emits quality_delta.

alan: Rollout commands examples for ops: 
rwctl declaration create --id fast-path-lowlatency --allowed fp8,int8 --min-quality 0.98 --stability soft --canary 2%
rwctl declaration disable --id fast-path-lowlatency --reason "regression observed"

mike: Important implementation note: don't let declaration enforcement be a blocking path for serving. If enforcement causes a hard failure, runtime must fallback to the previous safe profile. Enforcement modes: permissive (log + notify), enforce (reject), auto-fallback (pick safe alternative).

sara: UX ask for Console: show declaration health per route: traffic %, avg quality_delta, cost savings, and a link to recent shadow runs. Also surface recently used hardware classes and any manual overrides.

lucy: Security note: declaration store needs RBAC and audit logs. When a customer_override is toggled, record who, when, and reason.

jia: Telemetry schema draft: 
- declaration_id (string)
- selected_precision (string)
- decision_code (int)
- quality_delta (float)
- baseline_score (float)
- hw_class (string)
- trace_id (string)

mike: Action items: 
- mike: collect and publish microbench per-hardware class for fp8/int8/4bit (this week)
- jia: instrument telemetry fields + shadow-run harness (next sprint)
- lucy: RBAC + approval workflow proposal (EOW)
- alan: migration job spec + canary playbook (next Tue)
- sara: author declaration schema RFC and include enforcement modes (in progress)

deploy-bot: rollout created: declaration fast-path-lowlatency canary=2% started 2026-03-22T18:05:01Z

sara: If no objections I'll consolidate notes and open the schema PR. :thumbsup:

lucy: :thumbsup: please include sample audit workflow in the PR.

mike: fine with direction. keep an eye on 4bit tail latencies during canary.

jia: will start tests tomorrow.

sara: thanks everyone, will follow up with PR and assign reviewers.
